label: bug
file: src/ingest/parser.ts

The parser splits the file strictly on `"\n"` and never strips `\r`. Windows-originated CSVs (like the new accounting export tool finance just switched to) use CRLF line endings, so each line — including the header line — ends with a trailing `\r`. That makes the last header column come out as `"description\r"` instead of `"description"`.

In `assertShape`, this fails the `REQUIRED_COLUMNS.some((column) => !header.includes(column))` check for the header row itself (called with `index = 0`), which is why the error always reports "row 1" regardless of the file's actual content — it's failing on the header before any data row is even parsed. Opening the file in a spreadsheet doesn't show this because spreadsheet apps normalize line endings transparently.

Fix: normalize line endings (e.g. strip a trailing `\r` from each line, or split on `/\r\n|\n/`) in `parseStatement` before splitting into fields.
